page.layout: One page of running text in a single column; running head centred above the text; signature centred below the last line. The strip of text at the far left is the edge of the neighbouring page and is not transcribed.

main_text.p: educata est, & scholarum curam, litera- rum studia, doctorumque & veritati ad- dictorum hominum consuetudinem, fa- miliarem penè dixerim, in virili hac ad- huc aetate, & sub gravibus reipubl. publi- cique boni curis deponere nondum po- test. Neque etiam ignotum est, quanto- pere in eo elaboret & desudet Tua Cels. ut juvetus scholastica in sacra & profanâ literaturâ feliciter instituatur, & facili ra- tione, brevi item temporis spatio, uberri- mum ingenii cultum capere queat. Cu- jus rei testes locupletes sunt colloquia & collationes cum doctis viris; scriptiones privatę; lucubrationes itè, quas de theo- logicis, logicis, & philosophicis argumē- tis in lucem hactenus Tua edidit Cels. Neque illis scholis, quas in toto suo prin- cipatu per civitates omnes & oppida con- stitutas Tua habet Cels. contenta; scho- lam insuper illustrē, pro principum, co- mitum, & nobilium liberis Cassellis ape- ruit, cui non tantum undequaque doctis præceptoribus prospectū est; verùm ipsa etiam Cels. Tua docendo, disputando & declamando illam excolit atq; exornat, ut ad summam pro scholis, quæ sapientiæ tam divinæ, quàm humanæ officinæ sunt

page.notes: Long s was rendered as f in "Celf." and is transcribed as "Cels." per the long-s rule. "juvetus" is printed as such (possibly for "juventus"); kept as printed. The line "ut juvetus" and the word "juvetus" carry no [?] because the print is legible, but this may be a printing error. The paragraph runs on from the previous page (no indent at the top) and continues beyond this page, so it is marked cont="true" and the last line is not closed by a stop.
